PART A — how-to-read-a-water-meter.md: Lead B1 — content is fuller than electric-meter page, CCF conversion table is strongest section, source:lines 140-148. Lead B2 — sources are USGS glossary homepage and EPA WaterSense landing page, not specific metering docs, source:frontmatter. Lead B3 — example table uses 4,523 CCF (~3.4M gal) which is commercial/industrial scale, not residential — typo-suspect, source:line 142.

PART A — 08-time-of-use-electricity.md: Lead C1 — rate table is strongest asset but PG&E rates cited as 'Effective March 2026' may already be stale, source:lines 35-65. Lead C2 — dishwasher annual savings column ($66/$124/$80) doesn't factor TXU's 2,000 kWh cap, source:lines 70-80. Lead C3 — Kasa KP115 smart plug affiliate product says 'handles dishwashers' but most US dishwashers are hardwired, not plug-in, source:line 80 area.

PART A — tiered-electricity-rates-explained.md: Lead D1 — very short page (~150 lines), mostly 'go ask your utility' framework with no concrete tier example, high bounce (83.3%) + low TOP (18s) suggest reader mismatch, source:body. Lead D2 — unlike TOU page, shows no example rate table or sample calculation, source:body. Lead D3 — sources: only generic DOE PDFs, no utility-specific tariff examples, source:frontmatter.

PART B Sweep 1 — 'national average'/'average U.S' with dollar figures: 15+ occurrences across 9 files. National average rate cited as 17.30¢/kWh (2025), 17-18¢/kWh, 18.34¢/kWh, 18.4¢/kWh — inconsistent year references. 899 kWh/month cited as '2022 national average' in electric-bill-breakdown.md:61 but as current in how-to-lower-electric-bill-complete-guide.md:78.

PART B Sweep 2 — '$262'/'$430'/'$500': $262 as narrow-basket national average in 2026-utility-cost-index-by-state.md:37 and average-utility-bills-by-state-2026.md:22. $500-600/month in 02-average-utility-costs-2026.md:5 (no basket caveat). $430-500 as broad-basket in average-utility-bills-by-state-2026.md:22. Contradiction: 02-average-utility-costs-2026.md says '$500-600/month on utilities' without caveat, overlapping broad basket but not narrow basket.

PART B Sweep 3 — thermostat per-degree claims: 3 distinct pages with inconsistent percentages. how-to-lower-electric-bill-complete-guide.md:95: '1% of heating/cooling cost per 1°F' (rule of thumb, unsourced). mcf-vs-ccf-vs-therms-on-gas-bill.md:94: '2 degrees can save 1-3%' = 0.5-1.5%/°F. 30-sudden-spike-in-electricity-bill-no-usage.md:177: 'Each 10°F reduction ... saves 3% to 5%' = 0.3-0.5%/°F (water heater, different domain). No cross-references or sourcing for per-degree percentage.

PART B Sweep 4 — 'BLS'/'December 2026': single occurrence at 7-states-with-worst-utility-spikes-2026.md:38: 'inflation stayed elevated at 3.8% (BLS, December 2026)'. CRITICAL: Date is August 2026 — December 2026 BLS data does not exist yet. This is either a projection presented as fact or a fabricated citation. Significant credibility risk for AdSense remediation.
